note: Track pentatonic-positions (guitar-scales), step 8: all five positions of the minor pentatonic scale as one neck: the roots first, position after position to the metronome, along one string, then a 12-bar solo that moves. The old Key choice is now moves (any key, 70 to 90 bpm), named only as {{=key}} and {{=bpm}}; the positions are named with their scale the first time, and the {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: One key, the whole neck
exercise.why: The five positions are one scale cut into five pieces, and each piece holds its roots in the same places, so finding a root tells you which position your hand is in anywhere on the neck.

cells.text:
The neck below shows the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale in all five positions, with every note but {{1}} faded. Play each {{1}} from the lowest on the neck to the highest, and say which string it is on.
Practice until you can jump to any of them without counting frets.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Under it are the five positions of {{=key}} minor pentatonic, numbered from the lowest on the neck. Climb position 1 and come down position 2, climb position 3 and come down position 4, then climb position 5, one note per beat.
If you lose the next position, stop on a ringed {{1}} and find the position around it before you go on.

Play the scale along the G string alone, from its lowest note on the neck below to its highest and back.
Say the number of the position you are in each time your hand moves.
{{?key}}In another key the five positions slide along the neck together and stay in the same order.

Press Play below to start the backing track, a 12-bar blues in {{=key}} minor. Improvise, and start each new phrase in a position you have not just used.
Practice until moving along the neck feels no harder than staying where you are.
